A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoE-GS research work. Their complete main texts and appendices, including figures, tables and equations, are readable and support reliable comparison after matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original reconstruction experiments on N3V, Technicolor and HyperNeRF, alongside router, efficiency, distillation and expert-specialization analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains original benchmark experiments and additionally reports training-budget, repeated-training, motion-trajectory and fused-geometry evaluations.

M1.justification: The core expert/router training, weight splatting, pruning and distillation procedures remain unchanged. Appendix D adds a post-hoc procedure that lifts pixel gates into normalized Gaussian responsibilities, rescales opacities and concatenates experts for volumetric rendering without retraining. This is a limited additional inference procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use N3V, Technicolor and monocular HyperNeRF with the same reported scenes and reconstruction settings. The new budget, repeated-training and depth-consistency analyses examine retained coverage; they do not introduce a new dataset, population or input scenario.

E2.justification: Comparator membership in the retained benchmark and distillation tables is unchanged. Appendix F introduces best-of-five retraining as a comparison strategy for E-D3DGS, Ex4DGS and 4DGaussians, assessing whether their strongest individual runs can match MoE-GS.

E3.justification: v2 adds substantially different evaluation protocols: expert training at 100%, 50%, 20% and 10% of full wall-clock budgets; depth reprojection across ordered viewpoint pairs for fused Gaussian models; and paired MoE/expert retraining controls. These are additional experimental designs, rather than evidence that the retained benchmark experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds training-budget sensitivity, repeated-training stability and geometric-consistency analyses. Appendix E replaces v1's quantitative routing-weight analysis against optical flow and image gradients with expert motion-trajectory analysis. Appendix G mostly redisplays the weighting ablation already present in v1 Table 10 and is not an entirely new ablation.

E5.justification: v1 provides no repeated-run variability reporting. v2 Appendix F specifies five trainings per expert and five corresponding MoE trainings, with minimum, maximum and mean PSNR in Table 12. This introduces substantive uncertainty reporting, without establishing an increased run count for the retained experiments. No confidence intervals or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: All retained numerical tables preserve their values after renumbering. New results include 32.60 dB for MoE-GS at 20% training budget (Table 6), a 32.72–33.23 dB repeated-training range with 33.01 dB mean (Table 12), and depth-consistency and trajectory findings. The earlier routing-specialization results are removed. Table 13 additionally reports distilled E-D3DGS SSIM as 0.918, conflicting with 0.915 in v1 Table 10 and retained v2 Table 11.

T1.justification: The main method equations retain their mathematical content, with notation clarified. v2 adds Gaussian-responsibility, opacity-fusion and depth-consistency definitions in Equations 12–16, while removing v1's weighted-mean specialization definition. These are localized formal additions; no theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The central novelty, adaptive reconstruction and efficiency-component claims remain. The abstract and introduction explicitly distinguish the quality objective from FLOP reduction, while the conclusion adds claims about improved 4D consistency and Gaussian responsibilities supporting future geometric fusion.

C2.justification: v2 replaces the earlier dataset-dependent routing-specialization interpretation with detailed explanations of each expert's motion priors, strengths and failure conditions. It also introduces interpretations of Gaussian lifting as geometric integration, reduced-budget effectiveness, and repeated-training gains as evidence of complementary deformation priors rather than random variation.

D1.justification: New disclosures include near-zero directional/temporal weight initialization, explicit expert combinations, expert training times, router overhead and rendering implementation tradeoffs. The reported hardware changes from A6000 and 4090 GPUs to A6000 only, without establishing reruns. A project-page pointer for video demonstrations is also added.

R1.justification: The cited-work set and related-work sections are retained. v2 more explicitly positions MoE-GS's combination of heterogeneous deformation priors against the computational-efficiency purpose of sparse LLM MoEs, providing a limited refinement of research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 makes targeted abstract, introduction and conclusion revisions, expands the weight-splatting explanation, and updates appendix organization and cross-references. It also adds acknowledgments, author contact information and conference headers. Most existing exposition and the main section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 is substantially redesigned with MoE curves and motion visualizations. The earlier specialization scatter/flow display is removed, while depth-consistency Figure 10, trajectory Figure 11, and budget/stability tables are added. Table 13 redisplays an existing distillation comparison. These materially revise the visual evidence, beyond routine pagination and table formatting.

improvement.justification: The training-budget and paired five-run studies strengthen evidence about computational cost and run variability that v1 lacked, and the revised positioning clarifies the method's purpose. The benefit is limited by inconsistent expert-set descriptions between Section 4.1 and Appendix F, the conflicting distillation SSIM in Table 13, and removal of the earlier quantitative routing-specialization analysis. With the main benchmark evidence unchanged, the net improvement is useful but limited.
